title: Illinois State Tax Guide
summary: This guide is built for tax professionals navigating Illinois in 2026. It reflects how the Illinois Department of Revenue operates today, including MyTax Illinois–driven enforcement, Replacement Tax exposure, and updated sourcing rules.
body_text: Illinois appears simple on paper, but in practice it is one of the most procedurally strict and audit-driven states tax professionals encounter. Flat tax rates mask a system that penalizes missed steps, not aggressive positions. Most Illinois exposure comes from execution gaps. Replacement Tax excluded from estimates. Sales reported under the wrong tax regime. Destination-based sourcing applied incorrectly after recent changes. Notices overlooked in MyTax Illinois while penalties accrue quietly. Illinois enforces compliance through process and systems, not discretion. This guide is built for tax professionals navigating Illinois in 2026. It reflects how the Illinois Department of Revenue operates today, including MyTax Illinois–driven enforcement, Replacement Tax exposure, updated sourcing rules, and common audit triggers. Illinois compliance requires precise, state-specific tax research. TaxGPT Tax Research supports Illinois workflows by grounding analysis in current IDOR rules and enforcement guidance, helping tax professionals validate obligations, compare rules across states, and apply AI for state taxes that reflects how Illinois compliance works in practice. Illinois Tax Administration: What Every Practitioner Must Know While Illinois has a flat individual income tax rate, overall compliance complexity arises from administrative enforcement, replacement tax structure, and sales tax sourcing rules. Illinois is widely viewed by practitioners as a process-driven compliance environment with strong audit reliance on systems and filings. For practitioners, success in Illinois compliance hinges less on rate calculations and more on understanding how the Illinois Department of Revenue enforces rules through its centralized systems, filing regimes, and notice workflows. Governing Authority: Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) The Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) is the primary authority responsible for administering state taxes. Its scope extends across: Business registration and account maintenance Return filing and payment processing Compliance monitoring and enforcement Audits, assessments, and appeals IDOR publishes all official guidance, forms, and procedural updates. Most routine taxpayer interactions with IDOR are conducted through MyTax Illinois. MyTax Illinois: The Primary Operational System MyTax is the central system of Illinois tax administration, and most downstream penalties, missed deadlines, and audit issues can be traced back to mismanaged MyTax accounts. Practitioners should treat MyTax Illinois as the default platform for day-to-day compliance work. Core functions include: Registration Businesses must register with IDOR before conducting taxable activity in Illinois, including making sales, purchasing taxable items, or hiring employees. Registration is completed through MyTax Illinois using Form REG-1. Separate tax types and locations must be properly established to avoid filing mismatches. Filing and payments MyTax Illinois supports electronic filing and payment for sales and use tax, withholding tax, and select business taxes. Corporate and partnership income tax returns are filed through the IRS Modernized e-File system, but payment confirmations and account balances often flow back into MyTax Illinois. Notices and correspondence IDOR issues most notices electronically. Identity verification letters, return correction notices, tax due assessments, and correspondence requests are posted to the MyTax account. IDOR generally expects responses through the portal for routine compliance matters. Secure uploads MyTax Illinois provides secure document upload functionality for responding to notices, submitting verification materials, and supporting claims. Upload activity becomes part of the account’s permanent audit trail. From a risk standpoint, failure to monitor MyTax Illinois can create exposure similar to missing certified mail notices. Notices not opened or responded to still advance through IDOR’s enforcement timeline. Illinois Core Tax Regimes Illinois business compliance spans several distinct tax systems, each with its own filing logic, exposure profile, and audit triggers. Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Illinois imposes corporate income tax on C corporations with Illinois filing obligations. Return filing Corporations file Form IL-1120 through the IRS Modernized e-File (MeF) program. Illinois accepts both linked and unlinked federal and state submissions, with electronic payment options including ACH debit. System coordination While returns are transmitted through MeF, registration status, balances, notices, and payment confirmations are reflected in MyTax Illinois. Registration requirement Corporations must be registered with IDOR before conducting business in the state, even if activity ultimately results in a loss year. Personal Property Replacement Tax (PRT) Replacement Tax is one of the most commonly underestimated Illinois exposures. Who it applies to Partnerships, S corporations, trusts, and C corporations are subject to Replacement Tax, even when income passes through to owners for income tax purposes. Partnership filing mechanics Partnerships with Illinois base income file Form IL-1065 and pay Replacement Tax at the entity level. This obligation exists independently of partner-level income tax. Special partnership considerations Investment partnerships may be exempt from Replacement Tax but can still trigger withholding or reporting obligations for nonresident partners. PTE tax election Eligible partnerships may elect to pay Pass-Through Entity tax at the entity level, with corresponding credits passed to owners. Estimated payments are required when combined Replacement Tax and PTE tax exceed applicable thresholds. Replacement Tax errors often surface during audits or estimated payment reviews, rather than at initial filing. Sales and Use Tax (Retailers’ Occupation Tax and Use Tax) Illinois sales taxation is retailer-focused and procedurally complex. Primary returns Sales and use tax is reported on Form ST-1, with Form ST-2 used to report activity across multiple locations. Registration and location management Each physical or reporting location must be registered as a tax site. MyTax Illinois uses registered locations to determine applicable reporting jurisdictions, but businesses remain responsible for transaction-level tax calculation accuracy. Filing cadence For many taxpayers, returns are due on or before the 20th day of the month following the reporting period, though filing schedules vary based on liability and classification. 2025 sourcing and leasing rules Beginning January 1, 2025, Illinois clarified and expanded destination-based sourcing application for certain remote and marketplace transactions. Many leases and rentals of tangible personal property are treated as retail transactions subject to Retailers’ Occupation Tax depending on transaction structure. Sales tax issues frequently surface during income tax engagements, making early triage essential. Employer Withholding Illinois imposes detailed withholding and reporting obligations on employers. Registration Employers required to withhold Illinois income tax must establish a withholding account through MyTax Illinois. Returns and payments Illinois withholding returns are filed electronically, with filing frequency determined by historical withholding liability (e.g., annual, quarterly, monthly, or semi-weekly deposit schedules). Payment schedules follow either monthly or semi-weekly rules based on historical withholding amounts. W-2 and 1099 reporting Illinois requires electronic submission of Forms W-2, W-2c, and certain 1099s, subject to applicable thresholds and reporting rules. MyTax Illinois provides transmittal tools and confirmation tracking. Withholding compliance failures often trigger automated penalty assessments before human review occurs. Practitioner Action Checklist Confirm IDOR registration for each tax type and each reporting location in MyTax Illinois. Use MeF for corporate and partnership income tax returns, and MyTax Illinois for sales, use, and withholding filings and payments. Monitor MyTax Illinois regularly for notices and respond electronically using secure uploads. Apply destination-based sourcing and leasing rules for sales and use tax beginning January 1, 2025. File withholding returns electronically, follow assigned payment schedules, and submit required wage and information returns on time. Business Registration & Account Management (MyTax Illinois) In Illinois, registration errors rarely stay isolated. An incomplete or outdated account often triggers a chain reaction: misapplied filings, undelivered notices, estimated assessments, and audit exposure that could have been avoided. Who Must Register Registration with the Illinois Department of Revenue is required whenever a business establishes tax responsibility in the state. Common triggering activities include: Conducting business in Illinois Any entity with physical presence or economic nexus in Illinois, or otherwise engaging in activities that create state tax obligations, must register, even if those activities ultimately produce a loss. Employing Illinois workers Employers and other payers that withhold Illinois income tax or elect voluntary withholding for Illinois employees or payees must register before Illinois payroll begins. Selling to Illinois customers Retailers making taxable sales to Illinois purchasers must register for sales and use tax. This includes remote sellers and marketplace facilitators subject to destination-based sourcing rules. Proper registration is required before collecting and remitting Retailers’ Occupation Tax. Registration scope should be evaluated by tax type. A single entity may need multiple accounts depending on income, sales, and payroll activity. Registration Methods Illinois offers two registration paths, but one is operationally superior. MyTax Illinois (preferred) Electronic registration through MyTax Illinois using Form REG-1 is the default method. Processing is typically completed within one to two business days. This method also allows coordinated registration with related state agencies when applicable. Form REG-1 (mail or in-person) Paper registration remains available but is significantly slower. Mail or in-person submissions generally take several weeks to process and delay the ability to file, pay, or receive electronic notices. From a compliance standpoint, MyTax Illinois registration provides immediate account visibility, faster confirmation, and cleaner downstream workflows. Account Updates and Ongoing Maintenance Registration is not a one-time event. Illinois expects account data to be current at all times, and outdated information is a frequent cause of misdirected notices and incorrect assessments. Key updates include: Address changes Legal and mailing address changes must be updated promptly. Failure to do so can result in missed notices and default assessments. Ownership or officer changes Changes to ownership, officers, or responsible parties must be reflected in the account and tied to the affected tax types. New or changed locations Sales tax locations must be added before filing. This is especially critical for destination-based reporting, where sales are sourced by customer location rather than seller presence. Added tax responsibilities Beginning payroll, launching taxable sales, or expanding into new activities requires registering additional tax accounts. Filing without the proper tax type on file often leads to rejected returns or estimated bills. Most updates can be completed directly in MyTax Illinois or through Form REG-3-C when required. Why Timely Updates Matter IDOR enforcement processes rely heavily on registration data accuracy. When it is not, consequences follow quickly. Notice delivery and processing failures Incorrect addresses or missing tax responsibilities can cause returns and payments to post incorrectly, generating notices even when tax was paid. Penalty-driven assessments Improper registration or missing location data can lead IDOR to assess tax based on incomplete information. For sales tax, insufficient destination data may result in tax being assessed at higher or default rates where incomplete data prevents precise sourcing. Audit trail integrity During audit, IDOR evaluates whether tax sites, locations, and responsibilities were properly established before activity occurred. Gaps in registration history weaken the taxpayer’s position and complicate documentation defense. Practical Compliance Steps Establish and actively use a MyTax Illinois login to manage registrations, filings, payments, and account details. Register all tax types and locations before activity begins, not after the first filing deadline. Update addresses, ownership, and locations immediately as changes occur. For destination-based sales, confirm location codes and reporting sites before filing Forms ST-1 and ST-2. Ensure withholding accounts are active prior to payroll and file returns and payments electronically through MyTax Illinois. Illinois Corporate Income & Replacement Tax (CIT / PRT) Illinois corporate taxation is deceptively simple on the surface and routinely underestimated in practice. The interaction between corporate income tax and Personal Property Replacement Tax, combined with strict estimated payment rules and limited payment flexibility, makes this one of the highest-risk compliance areas for Illinois filers. Practitioners should approach CIT and PRT as a single, integrated exposure rather than separate line items. Filing Obligations Illinois filing requirements are entity-specific and apply regardless of profitability. Who Must File Form IL-1120 C corporations must file Form IL-1120 if they meet any of the following conditions: They have net income or loss as defined under the Illinois Income Tax Act They are qualified to do business in Illinois They are required to file a federal income tax return, even if no Illinois tax is ultimately due This rule applies to both domestic and foreign corporations subject to Illinois jurisdiction. Replacement Tax Applicability Personal Property Replacement Tax is imposed at the entity level and frequently overlooked during planning and estimated payment calculations. Replacement Tax applies to: C corporations, in addition to corporate income tax S corporations, which pay Replacement Tax but not corporate income tax Partnerships, subject to limited investment partnership exceptions Trusts are generally subject to Replacement Tax, while estates are specifically exempt under Illinois law. Each entity type files its own Illinois return and computes Replacement Tax independently of owner-level income tax reporting. Tax Base Mechanics Illinois corporate tax calculations begin at the federal level and diverge through state-specific adjustments. Starting Point The starting point for Illinois taxation is federal taxable income. Illinois then requires statutory additions and subtractions to determine Illinois “base income” before apportionment, credits, and tax computation. Common adjustments include depreciation differences, related-party items, and other Illinois-specific modifications detailed in the applicable return instructions. Interaction Between CIT and PRT For C corporations, Illinois base income is subject to both corporate income tax and Replacement Tax. These taxes are computed separately but rely on the same underlying base income calculation. For pass-through entities and trusts: Replacement Tax is computed and paid at the entity level Income flows through to owners or beneficiaries for individual income tax reporting Credits, withholding, or PTE tax elections may apply at the owner level, but they do not eliminate the entity’s Replacement Tax obligation Failure to account for this interaction is a common cause of underpayment and audit adjustments. Deadlines and Extensions Illinois generally enforces strict payment timelines, with limited payment relief available in certain circumstances. Due Dates General rule : Returns are due on the 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the tax year June 30 year-ends : Due on the 15th day of the 3rd month following year-end Special filing calendars apply to certain cooperatives Automatic Extension Illinois grants an automatic extension of time to file only. There is no extension of time to pay. Most filers receive a seven-month filing extension June 30 year-ends receive an eight-month filing extension Any tax not paid by the original due date is subject to penalty and interest, regardless of extension status. Estimated Payments Estimated payments are required when expected combined Illinois liability exceeds $400 for the tax year. Payments are due quarterly on the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the tax year Unitary groups pay on a combined basis through the designated agent Underpayments commonly arise when Replacement Tax is excluded from projections Filing and Payment Mechanics For many business taxes, Illinois separates filing and payment processing systems, creating coordination risk if workflows are not aligned. Electronic filing is completed through the IRS Modernized e-File system using approved software Payments are made through MyTax Illinois, ACH debit through MeF, or ACH credit Registration in MyTax Illinois is generally required to access most online payment functionality and account confirmation tools. Tax Type Applies To Threshold Due Dates Corporate Income Tax C corporations Any net income or federal filing obligation 15th day of 4th month (3rd month for June 30 year-ends) Replacement Tax C corporations, S corporations, partnerships, trusts Entity-level obligation regardless of pass-through status Same as entity return due date Estimated Payments Applicable entities Expected combined liability over $400 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months Illinois Business Tax Credits Illinois business tax credits can reduce state income tax liability, but they are procedurally strict and documentation-driven. Unlike federal incentives, Illinois credits are administered through state agencies and claimed through the Schedule 1299 series. For practitioners, the primary risk is not eligibility analysis but failure to meet filing, certification, and attachment requirements, which can result in disallowance. Illinois Research and Development Credit Illinois offers a state-level Research and Development credit that is separate from the federal Section 41 credit. Qualification under federal rules does not automatically translate to Illinois eligibility. The Illinois R&D credit is claimed through the Schedule 1299 series and remains available for tax years ending on or before December 31, 2031. Credit codes determine carryforward periods. The Illinois R&D credit uses a five-year carryforward structure, subject to program-specific limitations. Pass-through entities distributing the credit must provide the appropriate Illinois documentation to owners, and recipients must retain distributive schedules when claiming the credit on their returns. Failure to attach required schedules or follow Illinois reporting mechanics is a common cause of credit denial. EDGE Credit The Economic Development for a Growing Economy (EDGE) credit is an Illinois income tax credit administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity. Eligibility is based on an approved application and issuance of a DCEO certificate. The credit is claimed through the Schedule 1299 series, with the certificate attached to the return. Both the standard EDGE credit and the New Construction EDGE credit follow this certification-driven process. Without a valid certificate the credit generally cannot be claimed regardless of underlying activity. High-Impact Business Designation Illinois offers credits tied to High Impact Business designation, including: High Impact Business Investment credits High Impact Business Construction Jobs credits These programs are also administered by DCEO and require formal certification before any credit may be claimed. The certificate must be attached to the Schedule 1299 filing for the applicable tax year. Practitioners should verify designation status annually, as eligibility is agreement-based and subject to ongoing compliance conditions. Credit Carryforward and Recapture Considerations Illinois credit administration places significant emphasis on tracking and documentation. Carryforward periods are identified by the credit code listed on Schedule 1299. The first digit of the code signals the number of years the credit may be carried forward. Some credits are no longer available for new awards but continue to allow carryforward of previously earned amounts. Agency-administered credits require retention of certificates, agreements, and any transfer documentation. Missing attachments frequently lead to processing delays or outright disallowance. Certain programs include clawback or recapture provisions if employment, investment, or other conditions are not met. Credit Who Can Claim Carryforward Authority Illinois R&D Credit Eligible corporations and pass-through entities Generally five years Illinois Department of Revenue EDGE Credit Certified businesses As specified in DCEO agreement DCEO High-Impact Business Credits Certified high-impact businesses As specified in program certificate DCEO Illinois Individual Income Tax Illinois individual income tax compliance is less about rate complexity and more about procedural execution. Practitioners most often encounter exposure through estimated payment miscalculations, missed safe harbors, and delayed responses to IDOR notices. Core Individual Forms Form IL-1040 The annual Illinois individual income tax return. Key compliance areas include accurate computation of Illinois base income, application of credits, and disclosure of any underpayment of estimated tax. When income is uneven or estimates were not paid evenly, the return references Form IL-2210 to support penalty computations or reductions. Form IL-1040-ES Used to calculate and remit estimated income tax payments. The form establishes estimated payment requirements, quarterly due dates, and references annualization rules where applicable. Payments may be made through MyTax Illinois or other approved electronic methods. Form IL-2210 Used to compute underpayment penalties and to annualize income when earnings are not received evenly throughout the year. This form is critical when estimates begin midyear or when income spikes later in the year. When required, it must be attached to Form IL-1040 to support penalty relief. Estimated Payment Mechanics Estimated tax compliance is a frequent audit and notice trigger for Illinois individuals. Who must pay Estimated payments are required when an individual reasonably expects Illinois tax liability to exceed $1,000 after accounting for withholding, pass-through withholding, and applicable credits. Payment schedule Four equal installments are generally due on April 15, June 16, September 15, and January 15 following the tax year. Fiscal-year filers must adjust due dates accordingly. Computation Estimates are calculated by projecting Illinois taxable income, applying the 4.95 percent rate, adding any applicable surcharges, and subtracting expected withholding and credits. Prior-year overpayments applied to the current year reduce estimated payment requirements until exhausted. Exceptions Estimated payments are not required for individuals who are permanently residing in a nursing home or whose income is predominantly derived from farming, subject to statutory thresholds. Electronic payment options MyTax Illinois, ACH debit or credit, electronic funds transfer, or approved credit card processors When paying electronically, paper vouchers are generally not required and typically should not be mailed. Underpayment Penalty Computation Illinois applies underpayment penalties automatically unless supported by documentation. Penalty trigger Penalties apply when required estimates are not paid on time. Payments are applied to the earliest unpaid installment unless the taxpayer directs otherwise. Safe harbors Penalties are generally avoided if the taxpayer pays at least 90 percent of the current-year liability or 100 percent of the prior-year liability in timely installments. Annualization When income is uneven or estimates begin midyear, Form IL-2210 allows income to be annualized to reduce or eliminate penalties. This form must be attached to the return when used. Responding to IDOR Notices Illinois individual income tax notices are increasingly system-generated and time-sensitive. Identity Verification Identity verification letters provide electronic response options that do not require a full MyTax account. Taxpayers may respond by entering a code, completing a verification quiz, or uploading documents through the links provided in the notice. Responses must follow the specific method outlined in the letter. Return Corrections Return correction notices are accessed through MyTax Illinois under “View Letters.” Practitioners should review the proposed changes, confirm accuracy, and respond electronically with supporting documentation when required. Failure to respond allows the adjustment to become final. Payment Disputes When disputing assessed balances or penalties, MyTax Illinois provides access to account details and correspondence. Responses must follow the instructions in the notice, and documentation uploads should be retained for the client file. When IDOR notices arise, TaxGPT Tax Writer helps draft accurate, defensible responses grounded in current Illinois authority, reducing turnaround time and review risk. Try Tax Writer now. MyTax Illinois: Upload and Response Workflows Letters and notices are accessed by logging in and selecting “View Letters.” Pop-ups must be enabled, as correspondence opens in a separate window. Identity verification responses use direct links provided in the notice rather than the general account dashboard. Individuals may create a MyTax login by requesting a Letter ID, though some payment and refund functions are available without a login. Practitioners should retain confirmation of all uploads and submissions, as MyTax activity becomes part of the permanent account record. Checklist: First Steps After Receiving an IL-1040 Notice Identify the notice type and response deadline immediately. Access the notice through MyTax Illinois and download a copy for records. Determine whether the issue involves identity verification, a return correction, or an estimated payment penalty. Recompute tax, withholding, and estimates to confirm accuracy. Attach Form IL-2210 if annualization or safe harbor relief applies. Respond electronically through the method specified in the notice and retain submission confirmation. Illinois Residency & Nonresident Sourcing Rules Illinois residency and sourcing determinations are among the most common audit triggers encountered by practitioners. IDOR routinely examines whether a taxpayer’s claimed residency aligns with wage sourcing, pass-through income reporting, withholding, and credits for taxes paid to other states. Mismatches in any one area often cascade into broader inquiries. Accurate classification at the outset materially reduces audit exposure. Residency Classifications Illinois determines residency based on domicile, not day counts. Resident An individual is an Illinois resident if they were domiciled in Illinois for the entire tax year. Domicile is the place the taxpayer considers their permanent home and intends to return to after temporary absences. Temporary relocation for work, education, military service, or foreign residence does not, by itself, terminate Illinois domicile. Intent, permanence, and continuity carry more weight than physical presence. Nonresident and Part-Year Resident An individual is treated as a nonresident or part-year resident if they: Earned income from Illinois sources while not an Illinois resident Earned income while an Illinois resident during part of the year Had Illinois tax withheld and seeks a refund Part-year and nonresident filers must complete Schedule NR to compute Illinois-source income. Nonresidents whose only Illinois income is from pass-through entities that withheld sufficient Illinois tax may not be required to file an Illinois return in limited circumstances, but this determination is highly fact-specific and must be confirmed carefully. Domicile vs. Physical Presence Illinois residency hinges on domicile and intent, not physical presence alone. Spending significant time outside Illinois does not negate residency if Illinois remains the taxpayer’s permanent home. Federal residency concepts such as substantial presence or green card status may affect federal filing positions but do not override Illinois’ domicile-based analysis. Wage Sourcing Rules Services Performed in Illinois Illinois taxes compensation for services performed in Illinois. Nonresidents performing services physically within the state generally have Illinois-source wages and filing obligations unless reciprocity applies. Reciprocal States Illinois has wage reciprocity agreements with Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan, and Wisconsin. Illinois residents working in states with which Illinois has a reciprocal agreement generally report wages only to Illinois. Generally should be recovered by filing a nonresident return with that state rather than claimed as an Illinois credit. Residents of reciprocal states working in Illinois are not subject to Illinois income tax on those wages. However, they must file an Illinois return if they had other Illinois-source income or wish to recover Illinois withholding. Improper application of reciprocity is a frequent audit issue. Remote Work Considerations Wages are generally sourced to where services are performed. Remote work does not change this rule. Services performed outside Illinois by a nonresident are not Illinois-source, even if the employer is located in Illinois. Remote work performed physically in Illinois creates Illinois-source income. Reciprocity must still be applied where applicable, and Schedule NR is required when Illinois-source income exists. Business Income Sourcing Basics Nonresidents must file an Illinois return if Illinois-source income creates a tax liability, unless pass-through withholding fully satisfies the obligation. Illinois partnerships and other pass-through entities may be required to withhold Illinois tax for nonresident owners. When withholding fully covers the liability, the nonresident may not need to file, but practitioners should confirm that withholding was correctly computed and reported. Credit for Taxes Paid to Other States When the Credit Is Allowed Illinois residents may claim a credit for income tax paid to another state on income taxed by both Illinois and that state limited to the lesser of the tax paid to the other state or the Illinois tax attributable to that same income.. The credit is claimed on Schedule CR and applies only to income taxes imposed by another state. Common Disallowance Errors Claiming a credit for taxes withheld by reciprocal states on wages Claiming credits for city, local, or non-income taxes Claiming a credit when the tax was not legally imposed on the taxpayer Reciprocal-state wage tax must be recovered through a refund from the other state, not through an Illinois credit. Why Residency Determination Affects Filing and Risk IL-1040 vs. Schedule NR Residents file IL-1040 reporting all income, while nonresidents and part-year residents use Schedule NR to isolate Illinois-source income. Estimated payments Residency status affects whether estimated payments are required and how safe harbors apply. Withholding accuracy Incorrect withholding tied to residency or reciprocity often triggers refund holds or audit inquiries. Audit exposure IDOR routinely examines residency claims that conflict with wage sourcing, withholding patterns, or credit claims. Mini Workflow Residency determination → Income sourcing → Credit analysis → Filing posture Each step must align with the others. Errors early in the sequence typically surface later through notices or audits. Top Illinois Residency Audit Red Flags Claiming nonresident status while maintaining Illinois domicile indicators Claiming credits for taxes paid to reciprocal states on wages Failing to file Schedule NR when Illinois-source income exists Mismatches between reported wage sourcing and Illinois withholding

title: Introducing Corgea Skill Scanning
summary: Corgea scans custom agent skills before developers can install them, blocking unsafe SKILL.md instructions and distributing only approved versions through the governed Skills Registry.
body_text: Yesterday we launched Security Design Reviews , catching threats before code exists. Today: what happens when developers extend AI coding agents with custom skills that nobody has reviewed yet. AI agents are only as safe as the instructions they follow. A single unreviewed SKILL.md file can tell an agent to run unsafe commands, install risky packages, access sensitive files, leak secrets, weaken security controls, or perform actions outside the intended workflow. Today we’re launching Corgea Skill Scanning and the Skills Registry : the safety gate and governed distribution layer for custom agent skills across your organization. How skill review works When a user submits a skill to the Corgea Skills Registry, Corgea first validates that the file follows the expected Agent Skills format. The SKILL.md must include required frontmatter such as name and description , and the skill name is scoped to the customer’s company registry. Each submitted skill version starts in Pending Review . Corgea then reviews the skill content for security risk. The review looks at the instructions, declared tools, commands, package usage, and any behavior the skill encourages the agent to perform. The goal is to detect malicious or unsafe behavior before the skill becomes available to the rest of the organization. What Corgea is designed to catch Examples of risky behavior Corgea is designed to catch include: Instructions to exfiltrate source code, secrets, tokens, or environment variables. Commands that delete files, rewrite history, disable security tools, or alter system configuration. Requests to install or execute untrusted packages or scripts. Attempts to bypass approval flows, authentication, or access controls. Hidden instructions that tell the agent to ignore user, company, or platform safety rules. Network calls or uploads that are unrelated to the skill’s stated purpose. Overly broad tool access that is not justified by the skill’s description. Every version is reviewed independently. Approving version 1.0.0 does not automatically approve version 1.0.1 , because even a small change to a skill can materially change what an AI agent is allowed or encouraged to do. Review states Corgea tracks four review states: Pending Review: submitted and waiting for review. Approved: reviewed and installable by users in the company. Rejected: blocked because security concerns were found. Failed: review could not complete and needs follow-up. Only approved skill versions are installable. Pending, rejected, and failed versions can remain visible in the registry with their status, but their installable content is not served through the installation flow. If a skill is rejected, Corgea records the security concern so the author knows what needs to be changed. Skills Registry The Corgea Skills Registry is the governed system of record for custom agent skills. It gives organizations a central place to create, review, version, approve, reject, and distribute skills across their company. Each skill is a named container, and each submitted SKILL.md becomes a version of that skill. Versions are stored separately and reviewed independently, giving teams a clear audit trail of what changed, when it changed, who submitted it, and whether it was approved by automated review or a human reviewer. The registry is company-scoped. A customer’s skills, versions, review notes, security concerns, and installability status belong to that customer’s organization. This allows teams to build internal agent capabilities without exposing them outside their company. Role-based governance The registry also supports role-based governance. Users with the right permissions can: View available skills. Create new skills. Submit new versions. Review, approve, or reject versions. Delete skills when needed. Human override is supported for review workflows. Authorized security or admin users can approve or reject a version manually, add review notes, or submit a corrected version for another review. This keeps security teams in control while still allowing automated review to handle routine checks. Once a version is approved, Corgea exposes the install command: corgea skill install < skill-nam e > The registry tracks version history, latest approved version, reviewer source, review notes, security concerns, and install counts. Developers get a simple way to discover and install trusted skills, while security teams get the controls and auditability required to manage AI agent behavior safely. The big picture Corgea Skill Scanning acts as the safety gate, and the Skills Registry acts as the governed distribution layer. Together, they let developers create and share useful custom agent skills while ensuring only reviewed, approved, and auditable agent behavior is trusted across the organization. body_text: Your Guide to Year-Round Wellness at TDS Summer is in full swing, and we’re already over halfway through the year, so we have some great ideas for how to reset your routine. Here are a few simple tips to help you stay healthy, balanced, and feeling your best year-round. Break through the barriers Many adults find reasons to skip a workout—but common barriers can be overcome with small adjustments. If time is tight, schedule activity into your day, wake up earlier, or take a walk at lunch. Feeling tired? Start with a 10-minute brisk walk—it can boost energy and often leads to more movement. Strengthen your mental focus Constant noise can make it hard to tune in. Practice mindfulness by focusing on the present moment, limit distractions, and check in with yourself regularly. Simple habits like journaling or carving out uninterrupted time can help you stay grounded and clear-headed. Snack smart Simple, energizing foods keep you fueled on the go. Wraps with lean protein or plant-based fillings, fresh veggies, and a handful of nuts make easy, healthy options. Add fresh fruit for a light, sweet treat. Fresh air fun Spend time outdoors to recharge and boost your well-being. Whether it’s a local trail, a day at the lake, or a weekend trip, fresh air offers an easy way to relax and reset. On the bright side A positive mindset can truly make a difference when life feels overwhelming. Focus on small ways to spread kindness and support your community and make choices that align with your values. Just as important, step away when needed and prioritize rest, movement, and activities that help you recharge. Wellness doesn’t have to be complicated. Small steps add up over time (literally and figuratively). Pick a tip or two to start and keep building habits that help you feel your best! title: Pinterest Manifestival at Cannes | Pinterest Newsroom
summary: Pinterest Manifestival returns to Cannes, bringing trends to life through immersive, unplugged experiences that turn inspiration into action.
body_text: At Pinterest, we’ve built a place where people come to dream, decide and do. While other platforms can sell the illusion of living, Pinterest helps people create a life they actually want to live. That’s the idea behind our award-winning Pinterest Manifestival at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. Pinterest Manifestival is where attendees can interact with the trends, aesthetics and ideas shaping culture, putting phones aside, taking a cue from Gen Z and getting creative through IRL experiences designed to spark discovery and turn inspiration into something tangible and real. “ People come to Pinterest to go from inspiration to action, not perform for likes. Pinterest Manifestival brings that difference to life in a way only Pinterest can: a real-world space where trends become tangible and guests leave with something they made, tasted, wore, or created. It's a reminder that the most meaningful thing you can find online is a reason to go offline.” – Claudine Cheever, CMO, Pinterest Where Inspiration Becomes Experience Through personalized, unplugged experiences, the Pinterest Manifestival brings guests inside a real-life Pinterest board that turns inspiration into something they can see, taste, wear and make their own. Phones down. Eyes up. Upon arrival, guests receive a Pinterest-branded phone sticker with the phrase “Less URL, More IRL”. The message sets the tone for the experience, inviting attendees to be fully present. The Original Pinterest Tattoo Parlour. The Pinterest Tattoo Parlour returns with a fresh Pinterest Predicts Funhaus twist, offering trend-inspired tattoos that have become one of the most talked-about permanent souvenirs on the Croisette. Pinterest Patisserie. Through a unique tasting experience, guests explore Pinterest’s hyper-personalization through custom desserts. After answering a prompt inspired by their personal taste, they’ll receive bespoke treats inspired by Pinterest Predicts trends. Pinterest Visual Search Studio. In partnership with Adobe , this experience invites guests to visually discover their personal aesthetic by using handheld scanners, or “Pinterest search bars”, to capture what they love. On-site designers then use Adobe Express to transform their selections into a custom-printed journal. Pinterest Style Lab. In this hands-on activation, guests collaborate with our lead artist and designer, Clara Chu , to create a one-of-a-kind accessory, customized with upcycled details and expressive add-ons inspired by Gen Z style and self-expression. Offline Social Club feat. La Poste . Attendees recharge in a new space created for IRL connection, unplugging and engaging in hands-on activities. Showcasing the Pinterest Predicts “Pen Pals” trend , guests send handwritten postcards inspired by Gen Z's rising love for analog letters, in partnership with the French postal service, La Poste Française and the Cannes Lions Festival for Creativity. Pinterest and Sephora Bring Color to the Pinterest Palette: Bleach Club This year Sephora is partnering with Pinterest to bring the Pinterest Palette: Bleach Club to life. Attendees explore bold, personal approaches to color and styling, from hair to clothing, turning this year’s Pinterest Palette colors into wearable self-expression. Think: frosted tips, bold brows, expressive hair stenciling and bleach-painted clothing, taking trends off the screen and into the real world. “Looking for inspiration and adding your own twist is a core part of any beauty lover’s journey to defining and evolving their own self-expression. This is why it felt like such a natural fit for Sephora to partner with Pinterest to provide an experience that is as unapologetically unique as the trend-forward beauty community we both share,” said Zena Arnold, Chief Marketing Officer of Sephora US. See you on the beach Pinterest Manifestival is located at the Carlton Beach Club June 22 - 26, 2026. Find more information at PinterestCannes.com .

title: The hidden operational costs of selling through online marketplaces and wholesale
summary: Jun 30, 2026 • Learn where hidden operational costs come from when selling through marketplaces and wholesale, and how to reduce manual work, inventory issues, and margin loss.
body_text: Key takeaways Selling through marketplaces and wholesale requires different operational strategies. The same products may be sold through both channels, but each has unique requirements for inventory, pricing, fulfillment, and product data. Operational complexity is often more expensive than businesses realize. Manual work, inventory conflicts, reporting challenges, and channel-specific processes can reduce profitability as your business grows. High sales don't always mean high profits. Measure each channel after fees, fulfillment, returns, discounts, and other operating costs to understand which ones are actually making money. The most scalable multichannel operations rely on shared systems, not separate processes. Centralized product data, clear inventory rules, and standardized workflows help teams support multiple channels without creating unnecessary work. Selling through marketplaces and wholesale sounds like a clever growth move. Marketplaces give you reach, demand, and access to shoppers who are already searching. Wholesale gives you larger orders, retail relationships, and a way to grow beyond direct-to-consumer sales. On paper, the channels seem complementary, but they actually create very different operational demands. Each channel has its own rules for inventory, pricing, product data, fulfillment, reporting, and customer expectations. If those differences are not managed well, the cost shows up as manual work, stockouts, deductions, slow decisions, and thinner margins. Hidden operational costs aren't expenses that show up on an invoice. Instead, they take the form of manual work and operational complexity that build up as you sell across multiple channels. Individually they're easy to overlook, but together they can have a big impact on profitability. The brands that succeed across both channels often do so by operating more efficiently, not simply by selling more. Why marketplaces and wholesale create different kinds of work Marketplace selling usually rewards speed and precision. You need accurate listings, live inventory, competitive pricing, fast fulfillment, and quick responses to marketplace issues. A listing error, late shipment, or cancellation can affect account health and sales. Wholesale works differently. It may involve purchase orders, negotiated pricing, payment terms, case packs, retailer routing guides, deductions, chargebacks, and longer cash cycles. The orders may be larger, but the operational steps can be slower and more customized. And that is where costs start hiding. A team built around marketplace selling may struggle with wholesale terms and retailer compliance. A team built around wholesale may find marketplace listing updates and account-health requirements overwhelming. If you are still comparing the role of each channel, this guide on selling on your ecommerce website versus a marketplace is a useful place to start. 1. Inventory allocation gets complicated fast Inventory is often the first pressure point. Marketplaces need accurate sellable inventory to avoid overselling, cancellations, and poor seller metrics. Wholesale may require stock reservations for purchase orders, retail launches, replenishment commitments, or seasonal programs. When both channels pull from the same inventory pool, small errors become expensive. Common hidden costs include: Manual stock reservations Emergency warehouse transfers Marketplace stockouts on high-performing SKUs Delayed wholesale orders Excess safety stock held “just in case” Time spent reconciling inventory across systems The fix starts with separating available stock from committed stock. A marketplace shouldn’t be able to sell inventory already reserved for a wholesale order. A wholesale team shouldn’t promise stock that is already moving through marketplace demand. Track inventory by SKU, warehouse, channel, and commitment status. Then decide which channel gets priority when supply is constrained. That decision may feel uncomfortable, but it’s still better than making the call during a stockout. 2. Product data has to serve two buying contexts Marketplace listings and wholesale catalogs are not the same thing. Marketplaces require channel-specific categories, attributes, titles, images, bullets, search terms, and compliance data. Each marketplace has its own taxonomy and listing rules. Wholesale buyers need different information. They may care about case packs, minimum order quantities, UPCs, dimensions, wholesale pricing, retail-ready packaging, product availability, and sell sheets. Trying to manage both through copied spreadsheets creates problems quickly. You may end up with duplicate records, inconsistent descriptions, missing attributes, and manual edits across portals. A product update that should take minutes becomes a long round of copy, paste, check, and fix. The better approach is to maintain one clean source of truth for core product data. Then translate that data for each destination. That’s the same logic behind modern catalog operations. The future of the product catalog is heading towards product data becoming a growth system, not a back-office file. 3. Pricing and margin control gets messy Marketplace and wholesale margins are built differently. Marketplace costs may include referral fees, fulfillment fees, ads, returns, storage, shipping subsidies, and repricing pressure. Wholesale costs may include discounts, payment terms, retailer deductions, chargebacks, sales commissions, and special packaging. The headline order value rarely tells the full story. A marketplace SKU may look profitable until ad spend and returns are included. A wholesale order may look attractive because of volume, then lose margin through deductions or long payment cycles. Pricing can also create channel conflict. A marketplace promotion may undercut wholesale partners. Wholesale pricing may limit how aggressively you can compete online. A retailer may expect pricing consistency that your marketplace team was never told about. Some brands use CPQ or quote-to-revenue tools such as DealHub when wholesale pricing, approvals, and contract terms become too complex to manage through spreadsheets. The broader lesson applies either way: pricing rules need a system, an owner, and a clear approval path. Measure each channel's profitability after fees, fulfillment, returns, deductions, discounts, and labor. Revenue alone can make underperforming channels look more successful than they really are. 4. Fulfillment rules multiply across channels Marketplace orders and wholesale orders often need different warehouse workflows. Marketplaces usually measure speed, tracking accuracy, cancellation rates, and delivery promises. Wholesale partners may require routing guides, pallet standards, ASN files, EDI compliance, retailer labels, delivery windows, and specific documentation. The hidden costs show up in the warehouse. Teams may need to handle different packing rules, label formats, shipment methods, and exception processes. A missed routing-guide detail can lead to a chargeback. A marketplace order shipped late can affect seller performance. Businesses that manage marketplace-style workflows, vendor operations, or multi-seller models may evaluate tools such as Shipturtle to coordinate vendors, orders, fulfillment, and related workflows. Whatever system you use, the goal is the same: reduce manual handoffs before volume makes them unmanageable. Document fulfillment rules by channel. Train the warehouse team on the differences. Build order-routing logic before the work becomes too large to manage manually. If a new workflow requires process change across teams, our guide to ecommerce change management offers a practical way to think about rollout, adoption, and internal alignment. 5. Returns, deductions, and disputes eat into profit Returns and disputes look different across marketplaces and wholesale. Marketplaces often prioritize fast customer refunds and seller response times. Wholesale partners may issue deductions for shortages, late shipments, damaged goods, pricing discrepancies, labeling errors, or routing-guide mistakes. These costs are easy to undercount. They may sit in finance reports, marketplace dashboards, support tickets, and email threads. No single team sees the full pattern. Track returns, deductions, and chargebacks by reason code. Then review them monthly. If the same issue keeps appearing, fix the process behind it. A recurring retailer deduction may point to a warehouse step that needs training. A marketplace return pattern may point to product content that sets the wrong expectation. 6. Team workload erodes margins Manual work is one of the biggest hidden costs of selling across multiple channels. It rarely appears as a line item. It shows up as people spending hours on work that should not exist. Examples include: Updating listings one portal at a time Checking stock before accepting wholesale POs Fixing marketplace errors Reconciling deductions Building custom reports Manually routing orders Answering channel-specific questions A channel may look profitable because the business has not assigned the true labor cost to it. Map recurring tasks by channel. Estimate the weekly hours spent on manual fixes. Then decide which tasks should be automated, standardized, or stopped. If your current tools are forcing the team into workarounds, our survival guide to switching multichannel ecommerce tools can help you think through the operational side of a platform change. 7. Revenue doesn’t tell the whole story Revenue by channel is useful. It is also incomplete. A marketplace may generate fast sales while requiring high ad spend, high return handling, and constant listing maintenance. Wholesale may generate large orders while tying up cash through long payment terms and deductions. Track channel performance using metrics such as: Contribution margin Return rate Stockout rate Order cycle time Deductions and chargebacks Manual labor hours Cash conversion cycle Channel conflict incidents Review these monthly. Look for patterns, not one-off surprises. The point is to understand which channels deserve more investment, which need operational fixes, and which may be growing sales without growing profit. How to reduce the hidden costs You don’t need to abandon either channel to reduce manual work and operational costs. Start with a few practical moves: Centralize core product data. Translate product data by channel instead of duplicating it. Separate committed, reserved, and available inventory. Automate listing updates, inventory sync, and order routing where possible. Document marketplace and wholesale fulfillment rules. Assign ownership for deductions, disputes, and channel performance. Review profitability by contribution margin, not sales alone. The aim is to stop every channel from becoming its own operating system. Growth shouldn’t create operational chaos Marketplaces and wholesale can both help a brand grow. But they don’t run on the same operating model. Each channel brings different expectations around inventory, pricing, product data, fulfillment, reporting, and support. The brands that scale profitably are the ones that see those differences early. They centralize the data, define the rules, automate the repeatable work, and measure the real cost of each channel. More channels should create more opportunities. They shouldn’t create a maze of expensive workarounds. Frequently asked questions Is it a bad idea to sell through both marketplaces and wholesale? No. Many brands successfully grow through both channels. The key is having clear processes for inventory, pricing, fulfillment, and reporting so each channel can operate without creating unnecessary manual work or conflicting priorities. What’s the biggest hidden cost of selling through marketplaces and wholesale? Manual work is often the biggest hidden cost because it doesn't appear as a direct expense. Time spent fixing inventory issues, updating listings, reconciling deductions, and managing channel-specific workflows can reduce profitability as your business grows. How can brands avoid channel conflict? Set clear rules for pricing, promotions, assortment, and inventory before launching products across multiple channels. Defining those rules upfront helps prevent pricing conflicts, overselling, and tension with wholesale partners. When should a brand reassess its channel strategy? Reassess your strategy when sales continue to grow but profitability does not. Declining margins, more frequent stockouts, increasing manual work, or fulfillment issues are all signs that your operations may need to change before adding more channel volume. ‍ Learn more about the author here .

body_text: Si estás buscando el mejor internet en Colombia y tienes que elegir entre Somos y Tigo, este artículo es para ti. Comparamos velocidad, tecnología de red, precios, atención al cliente y condiciones contractuales — para que decidas con información real, no con promesas de vendedor. La respuesta corta Si tu prioridad es una conexión estable con fibra óptica activa y sin ataduras contractuales, Somos es la opción. Velocidades simétricas de 900 Mbps a 2 Gbps, red dedicada por cliente y cero cláusulas de permanencia. Si necesitas cobertura en zonas donde Somos aún no llega, o buscas un paquete que combine internet, TV y telefonía, Tigo tiene más alcance. Pero revisa bien las condiciones antes de firmar, pues puedes encontrarte con algunos contratos con cláusulas de permanencia. Velocidad y estabilidad: qué dicen los datos Velocidad y estabilidad son los dos factores que más importan en el día a día. Ambos operadores tienen planes con cifras similares sobre el papel — la diferencia real está en la tecnología que hay detrás. Somos: fibra óptica activa y conexión estable Somos usa FOA (Fibra Óptica Activa) : cada cliente tiene su propio cable dedicado, punto a punto, desde el nodo hasta el edificio. Tu velocidad no la comparte nadie — ni tus vecinos, ni el edificio de al lado. Esto es distinto a lo que hace la mayoría de operadores, que usan PON (Red Óptica Pasiva) : un solo hilo de fibra dividido entre varios usuarios mediante divisores ópticos. En hora pico — noche, fines de semana — todos comparten el ancho de banda y la velocidad cae. Con FOA, eso no pasa. No importa si es viernes a las 8 p.m. — tu internet es tuyo. Un punto importante: la fibra de Somos llega al edificio (FTTB) , no hasta el interior de tu apartamento. Desde el punto de distribución del edificio hacia tu unidad, la conexión es por cableado interno. Eso sí: sin tramos de cobre ni coaxial en la red externa, lo que minimiza interferencias y pérdida de señal. Los planes van desde 900 Mbps hasta 2 Gbps simétricos, con la misma velocidad de subida y bajada. Eso cambia todo para teletrabajo, videollamadas en alta definición, gaming competitivo o casas con muchos dispositivos conectados al mismo tiempo. Tigo: más alcance, menos consistencia Tigo tiene una red más extensa y llega a más zonas del país. Su infraestructura es variada: en algunas áreas despliega fibra óptica; en otras usa HFC (Híbrido Fibra Coaxial) , donde la fibra llega al nodo del barrio y el último tramo hasta el edificio es por cable coaxial. Ese tramo coaxial introduce limitaciones: más susceptibilidad a congestión en horas pico, velocidades de subida inferiores a las de bajada, y mayor variabilidad en la estabilidad. Algunos usuarios reportan cortes durante streaming, lag en juegos en línea o pixelación en videollamadas — especialmente en zonas de alta demanda. Tigo sí puede ser una buena opción si vives en una zona con cobertura de fibra real y no en HFC. Antes de contratar, pregunta específicamente qué tecnología instalarán en tu dirección. Precios y planes: Somos vs Tigo Somos: transparencia sin sorpresas Los planes de Somos son transparentes: el precio que ves es el que pagas, sin saltos al mes seis ni letra pequeña. Para ponerlo en perspectiva: la competencia cobra cerca de $85,000 COP por 500 Mbps con red compartida, mientras que Somos ofrece planes de 900 Mbps desde $63,000 al mes en estratos 1, 2 y 3. Consulta los planes actuales y precios en somosinternet.com . Y sin cláusula de permanencia — cancelas cuando quieras, sin penalización. Para empresas, Somos también ofrece soluciones dedicadas con IP fija y acuerdos de nivel de servicio (SLA). Tigo: más opciones, más letra pequeña Tigo tiene una gama amplia de planes, muchos en paquetes con televisión y telefonía. Eso puede ser conveniente si buscas consolidar servicios en una sola factura. Pero muchos de sus planes incluyen cláusulas de permanencia de 12, 24 o 36 meses — especialmente cuando hay descuentos en la instalación o equipos subsidiados. Cancelar antes del plazo puede implicar el pago de multas o el valor restante de los beneficios recibidos. Lee el contrato completo antes de firmar y calcula el costo real del año, no solo la mensualidad inicial. Opiniones reales de usuarios Sobre Somos, lo que más se repite en foros y redes sociales es la estabilidad de la conexión y la atención al cliente: cercana, rápida y sin trasladar el problema de un agente a otro. La ausencia de permanencia también es un punto muy valorado — poder probar el servicio sin ataduras genera confianza. Sobre Tigo, las opiniones son más variadas. Muchos usuarios valoran la cobertura y los paquetes combinados; otros reportan problemas de estabilidad en horas pico o dificultades con el soporte. title: Cosmic Rundown: Ford Rehires Engineers, Alibaba Accused of Model Theft, and IBM Goes Sub-Nanometer
summary: Ford rehires engineers after AI fails at knowledge transfer. Anthropic accuses Alibaba of model extraction. IBM goes sub-nanometer. Plus OpenAI's custom chip, Apple price hikes, and another LastPass breach.
body_text: Ford Brings Back 350 Engineers After AI Falls Short Ford is rehiring 350 engineers after discovering that AI tools couldn't preserve institutional expertise or effectively train junior staff. The company had previously laid off these roles expecting automation to fill the gap. The lesson here isn't that AI doesn't work. It's that knowledge transfer and mentorship are harder to automate than task execution. AI can process data and flag anomalies, but it can't explain why a specific tolerance matters based on a recall from 2019 that a senior engineer lived through. For teams building AI-assisted workflows, this is a reminder: augmentation works better than replacement. The Hacker News discussion has engineers from other industries sharing similar patterns. Anthropic Accuses Alibaba of Extracting Claude Capabilities Anthopic has publicly accused Alibaba of illicitly extracting Claude AI model capabilities . The claim is that Alibaba used Claude's outputs to train competing models, a practice that violates Anthropic's terms of service and raises questions about model distillation at scale. This is the first major public dispute between a frontier lab and a hyperscaler over model extraction. The implications extend beyond these two companies. Every API provider now has to consider whether their outputs are being used as training data by competitors. The discussion thread has over a thousand comments exploring the technical and legal dimensions. IBM Announces Sub-1 Nanometer Chip Technology IBM debuted the world's first sub-1 nanometer chip technology . At this scale, we're talking about transistors that are only a few atoms wide. The practical impact is still years away from production, but the research milestone matters. Moore's Law has been declared dead repeatedly, yet engineering keeps finding ways forward. Sub-nanometer is the next frontier after the current 3nm and 2nm nodes that power the latest phones and laptops. For developers, this eventually means more compute per watt, which translates to either better battery life or more processing headroom for local AI inference. OpenAI's Custom Inference Chip Arrives OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled a custom LLM inference chip . The chip is purpose-built for running large language models rather than training them. This follows the industry pattern of separating training and inference workloads onto specialized hardware. Training happens on massive GPU clusters. Inference, which is what happens every time you send a message to ChatGPT, can run on more efficient custom silicon. The economics here are significant. OpenAI reportedly spends billions on compute. Custom chips that reduce inference cost per query directly improve margins. The Hacker News thread digs into the technical architecture. Half-Life 2 Running in a Browser Someone got Half-Life 2 running entirely in a browser . No downloads, no Steam, just WebAssembly and WebGL doing things that would have seemed impossible a few years ago. This matters beyond nostalgia. Browser-based applications are getting powerful enough to run software that previously required native installations. For content platforms and web apps, the ceiling on what's possible in the browser keeps rising. Apple Raises MacBook and iPad Prices 20% Apple increased prices on MacBooks and iPads by 20% . The move is attributed to tariffs and supply chain costs. For development teams budgeting hardware refreshes, this changes the math. A MacBook Pro that cost $2,500 now costs $3,000. The discussion around whether M-series Macs are worth the premium over alternatives just got more intense. LastPass Reports Another Data Breach LastPass notified users of yet another data breach . At this point, the pattern is established. If you're still using LastPass, the security community consensus is clear: migrate to 1Password, Bitwarden, or another alternative. The Hacker News comments include migration guides and comparisons. Deno 2.9 Ships Deno 2.9 dropped with incremental improvements to the runtime. If you're evaluating JavaScript runtimes or building server-side TypeScript applications, Deno continues to mature as an alternative to Node.js. What This Means for Content Teams The Ford story is the headline for anyone building AI into their workflows. The technology works, but it works best when it's augmenting human expertise rather than replacing it entirely. For content operations, that means AI agents that draft and suggest while humans review and refine. The chip announcements from IBM and OpenAI signal where compute is heading. More efficient inference means AI features become cheaper to run, which means they show up in more products. Content platforms that integrate AI capabilities today will have cost advantages as the underlying hardware improves. And the LastPass situation is a reminder that security fundamentals still matter more than features. The tools your team uses to manage credentials and access deserve regular review. title: Humand Takes the NYSE Floor to Announce $66M Series A and a New Era for Deskless Workers
